topic: Stresses and strains, theory of torsion and flexure
source: structure 1-70 / 71-140 / 141-228 updated.json (merged from old LEVEL 7 archive)

questions.q: 1. The direction of shear stress is
questions.explain: Shear stress can act in both horizontal and vertical planes depending on the loading conditions and the orientation of the cross-section being analyzed.

questions.q: 2. The direction of normal stress is
questions.explain: By definition, normal stress acts perpendicular (normal) to the surface of the cross-section or failure plane.

questions.q: 3. The direction of shear stress is
questions.explain: Unlike normal stress, shear stress acts tangential or parallel to the surface of the plane.

questions.q: 4. The actual numerical value of tensile stress (engineering stress) is .............. than the theoretical stress
questions.explain: Engineering stress is calculated using the original cross-sectional area, whereas theoretical (true) stress accounts for the reduction in area during tension.

questions.q: 5. Allowable stress in steel is less than
questions.explain: For safety, the allowable or working stress is always kept significantly lower than the yield stress of the material to prevent permanent deformation.

questions.q: 6. According to Hook's law, which one is wrong?
questions.explain: Hooke's Law states Stress = E × Strain. Therefore, MoE × Stress = Strain is mathematically incorrect.

questions.q: 7. Stress is directly proportional to strain within elastic limit is given by
questions.explain: This fundamental principle of elasticity was established by Robert Hooke.

questions.q: 8. Elasticity of a body is defined
options: the property by which a body returns to its original shape after removal of load
the property by which a body don't returns to its original shape after removal of load
the property by which a body undergoes deformation even after removal of load
questions.explain: Elasticity is the physical property that allows a material to return to its original dimensions after the unloading process.

questions.q: 9. Elasticity of a body is
options: the ratio of stress to strain
the resistance to the force acting
questions.explain: Elasticity represents the internal resistance of the material molecules to being separated by an external force.

questions.q: 10. Permanent set is
options: the force which acts permanently on the body
the shape of the member just after completion of construction
ratio of poisson's ratio to young's modulus
questions.explain: Permanent set refers to the plastic deformation that remains in a body after the applied stress is removed.

questions.q: 11. Stress in a member subjected to a force is
options: the ratio of modulus of elasticity to strain
the product of modulus of elasticity and strain
the resistance to the force acting
sum of strain and modulus of elasticity
questions.explain: According to the constitutive relation σ = Eε, stress is the product of the modulus of elasticity and strain.

questions.q: 12. Young's modulus is the ratio of the normal stress to the
options: reciprocal of normal strain within elastic limit
questions.explain: Young's modulus is valid only within the proportional limit where the stress-strain curve is linear.

questions.q: 13. Modulus of rigidity is the ratio of
questions.explain: The modulus of rigidity (G) is the ratio of shear stress to the corresponding shear strain.

questions.q: 14. In any member of structure system, the strain does not effect the size of member
questions.explain: Shear strain involves a change in shape (angle) rather than a change in dimensions or volume.

questions.q: 15. Plasticity of a body is
options: the ratio of stress to strain
questions.explain: While elasticity allows recovery of shape, plasticity is the property that allows permanent deformation.

questions.q: 16. The ratio of lateral strain to longitudinal strain is called
questions.explain: Poisson's ratio is a dimensionless constant representing the ratio of transverse contraction to longitudinal extension.

questions.q: 17. The product EI is called
questions.explain: The product of Young's modulus (E) and Moment of Inertia (I) defines the bending resistance of a beam, known as flexural rigidity.

questions.q: 18. The value of possion's ratio always remains
questions.explain: For most engineering materials, Poisson's ratio typically ranges from 0 to 0.5, thus remaining less than one.

questions.q: 19. The percentage elongation of a material from a direct tensile test indicates
questions.explain: High percentage elongation is a primary indicator that a material is ductile and can undergo significant plastic deformation.

questions.q: 20. The percentage reduction of a material from a direct compressive test indicates
questions.explain: Similar to elongation in tension, reduction in cross-sectional area in compression is a measure of ductility.

questions.q: 21. The safe value of stress below which the material will not fail when subjected to reversal of stress is known as
questions.explain: Endurance limit is the maximum stress that a material can withstand for an infinite number of cycles without failure.

questions.q: 22. The property by which the metals deforms continuously at a slow rate without further increase in stress is called
questions.explain: Creep is the time-dependent permanent deformation that occurs under constant stress, usually at high temperatures.

questions.q: 23. Toughness is
options: ability to absorb energy during plastic deformation
questions.explain: Toughness represents the total energy a material can absorb before it actually fractures.

questions.q: 24. The impact tests are used to determine
questions.explain: Tests like Charpy and Izod measure the energy absorbed during impact, which defines the toughness.

questions.q: 25. The ratio of maximum instantaneous stress due to sudden loading to the maximum stress due to gradual loading will be
questions.explain: Stress produced by a suddenly applied load is twice the stress produced by the same load applied gradually.

questions.q: 26. What is tenancy?
questions.explain: Tenacity (often misspelled as tenancy) refers to the ultimate tensile strength of a material.

questions.q: 27. At ordinary temperatures, how is the yield point affected with rate of loading?
questions.explain: At normal room temperatures, the rate of loading has a negligible effect on the observed yield point.

questions.q: 28. Simple bending equation is
questions.explain: This is the standard Euler-Bernoulli bending equation relating moment, inertia, stress, and curvature.

questions.q: 29. Stress in a beam due to simple bending is
questions.explain: Bending stress is directly proportional to the distance from the neutral axis (y).

questions.q: 30. In a composite bar the load distribution among different materials of which it is made is based on the assumption the all the materials will have
questions.explain: In composite bars, the primary assumption for compatibility is that all components undergo the same amount of strain.

questions.q: 31. The stress due to temperature change in a member depends on
questions.explain: Thermal stress only develops if the expansion or contraction is restricted by the support conditions.

questions.q: 36. Find the elongation of a rod if a load of p is applied on a rod having length, l c/s area, A and modulus of elasticity, E
questions.explain: The standard formula for axial deformation is derived from Hooke's Law (σ = Eε), where strain ε = Δl/l and stress σ = p/A.

questions.q: 37. Find the modulus elasticity of bar material (E) if c/s area of bar is A, length L, applied load P and elongation is Δ
questions.explain: Rearranging the elongation formula Δ = PL/AE to solve for E gives E = PL/AΔ.

questions.q: 38. The amount of stress developed due to increase in temperature in case of SSB if l=10m, ΔT=10°C, A=5cm²
questions.explain: In a Simply Supported Beam (SSB), the beam is free to expand or contract. Since there is no restriction to thermal expansion, no thermal stress is developed.

questions.q: 39. A member having cross section 5 cm × 5 cm is subjected to a tensile stress of 100 kg/cm², then the applied load should be
questions.explain: Load = Stress × Area. Area = 5cm × 5cm = 25cm². Load = 100 kg/cm² × 25cm² = 2500 kg.

questions.q: 40. Torsion is produced in a beam due to
options: eccentricity of load from centroidal axis
questions.explain: Torsion occurs when a load is applied at a distance (eccentricity) from the longitudinal centroidal axis, creating a twisting moment.

questions.q: 41. Due to torsion moment beam get
questions.explain: While bending moments cause curvature (bending), torsional moments specifically cause the cross-sections to rotate or twist relative to each other.

questions.q: 42. Torsional equation is given by
questions.explain: This is the standard torsion formula relating torque (T), polar moment of inertia (J), shear stress (τ), radius (R), modulus of rigidity (C), angle of twist (θ), and length (l).

questions.q: 43. The amount of temperature stress is .......... in fixed beam if compared with propped cantilever.
questions.explain: A fixed beam provides total constraint at both ends, whereas a propped cantilever may allow some relief of stress depending on the specific support conditions and degrees of freedom.

questions.q: 45. Stress concentration near the void is ................ as compared to solid portion.
questions.explain: Voids or discontinuities disrupt the flow of stress lines, causing them to 'bunch up' and increase the local stress intensity.

questions.q: 46. Hoop stress is
questions.explain: In thin-walled cylinders under internal pressure, hoop stress acts along the circumference and is tensile in nature.

questions.q: 189. The percentage of elongation of a material with applied direct tensile test is:
questions.explain: While percentage elongation is a measure of 'Ductility', the answer key provided marks 'Rupture' (c); elongation is measured until the point of rupture/failure.

questions.q: 191. In general equation for the deflection of the beam: M=EI* where EI is
questions.explain: EI represents the flexural strength.

questions.q: 192. When the load does not pass through the shear centre of the steel beam. It produces
options: torsional moment along with bending moment
questions.explain: Loads not passing through the shear center cause twisting (torsion) along with normal bending action.

questions.q: 201. Prestressing to a large extent removes the disadvantages which a conventional reinforced concrete structure suffers as compared to a comparable :
questions.explain: Prestressing allows concrete to span longer distances and remain crack-free, making it competitive with steel structures.

questions.q: 203. The load, required to produce a unit deflection in a spring is called :
questions.explain: Stiffness (k) is defined as Force per unit displacement (F/δ).

questions.q: 204. Force is the product of
questions.explain: According to Newton's Second Law, F = m·a.

questions.q: 208. At the yield point of a steel test piece :
options: materials behave in an elastic manner
materials regain its original shape on removal of load
questions.explain: Beyond the yield point, the material transitions from elastic to plastic (permanent) deformation.

questions.q: 209. Strain in concrete at zero stress is called :
questions.explain: Creep is the time-dependent deformation of concrete under sustained load, often continuing after stress is removed.

questions.q: 216. The Young's modulus of elasticity of steel is
questions.explain: The standard value for steel modulus (E) is 200 GPa or 200 kN/mm².

questions.q: 217. Creep of material is the property indicated by
options: elongation of the materials caused by changes in material properties
time dependent strain of the materials
shortening caused by shrinkage of the member
decrease in volume of the materials affected by the weather conditions
questions.explain: Creep is specifically defined as permanent deformation under a constant load over time.

questions.q: 218. The shear center may be defined as
options: the point through which the resultant of the shear stress pass
the point about which the moment of shear flow is zero
the centre of gravity of section
questions.explain: The shear center is the point where a load produces only bending and no torsion.

questions.q: 219. The shear center in the case of T-beam section is
options: at the C.G. of the section
at the neutral axis of the section
on the C.G. horizontal plane and away from C.G. within the leg projections
questions.explain: For sections with one axis of symmetry, the shear center lies on that axis. In a T-beam, it is typically at the junction of the web and flange.

questions.q: 220. The shear flow in a section can be defined as
options: total shear stress at a point
questions.explain: Shear flow (q) is the shear force per unit length along a cross-section (q = τ·t).

questions.q: 221. When a thin cylindrical shell is subjected to internal fluid pressure, which of the following stress is developed in its wall ?
questions.explain: Internal pressure in cylinders creates both hoop (circumferential) and longitudinal stresses.
